title: Dustwallow Marsh
body: Dustwallow Marsh is a fog-bound swamp on the eastern coast of Kalimdor, its western hills dividing it from the Barrens and the sea washing its shores to the north and east. Raptors, spiders, crocolisks and murlocs prowl its reeds, and for ages the marsh belonged to its beasts and to the Stonemaul ogres. Then, after the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore brought the survivors of her expedition to this coast and raised the island city of Theramore, guarded by watchtowers along the road west. The peace has never been easy. Daelin Proudmoore fell at Theramore when his fleet came against the Horde, and some of his loyal marines have since deserted their posts. The Stonemaul ogres, driven from their southern village by black dragonkin, now hold Brackenwall Village for the Horde, and in the Wyrmbog to the south Onyxia, daughter of Deathwing, broods in her lair.

title: Theramore Isle
body: Theramore stands on a rocky isle off the coast, a walled city of stone founded by the humans, dwarves and high elves who followed Jaina Proudmoore to Kalimdor after the battle of Mount Hyjal. Her mage tower rises at its heart, Foothold Citadel to the east, and the docks reach out into Dustwallow Bay, where Kul Tiras marines come and go on their monthly pay. A cook gathers swamp recipes for his uncle's restaurant in Stormwind, and the physicians of Alliance Trauma train their surgeons here. Just north of the gates lies the city's graveyard.

title: Foothold Citadel
body: Foothold Citadel is the great stone barracks of Theramore, standing east of Lady Jaina's tower with training grounds at its doors, where guards spar against dummies and drill under their combat masters. Commander Samaul, entirely loyal to his lady, commands her forces from within. On the top floor Captain Garran Vimes runs the city guard and its investigations, Adjutant Tesoran keeps the records of every soldier and every piece of equipment, and Clerk Lendry answers questions about the citizens. The guards here call themselves the finest Alliance soldiers in Kalimdor, sworn to uphold Alliance law so far from home.

Captain Wymor commands the post. Theramore has struggled to keep a presence in the marsh at all, and it is through watchtowers like this one, strung along the road, that the city keeps one.

title: Dreadmurk Shore
body: The Dreadmurk Shore runs north of Theramore's walls, a coast of mud flats, reeds and offshore islets where Mirefin murlocs keep their camps, their oracles and coastrunners crowding the beaches. The hulking Mudrock turtles that crawl the sand are hunted by Theramore's cooks for their tongues, the forked ones above all, which are said to have a flavor of their own. Fish school in the shallows, and the tide washes up wreckage among the reeds.

title: Alcaz Island
body: Alcaz Island lies off the northeastern coast, a lush, tropical isle ruled by the Strashaz naga. Sirens, myrmidons and great hydras guard its shores, and the Tidelord Rrurgaz commands them from behind barred gates. The naga are not alone. The criminal mastermind Doctor Weavil, sworn enemy of the seer Narain Soothfancy, has landed his flying machine here with a band of minions. The bloodkelp the naga gather is sought by those who practice divination.

Darkfang spiders creep through its reeds, and herbs grow thick by the water. At its heart stands Swamplight Manor, a lonely house whose current master, the hermit called Swamp Eye Jarl, asks travelers to help with his cooking.

From here the most warlike of the tauren clans raid the road and the towers of Theramore, and they cage the human soldiers they capture. Judging by the size of its raiding parties, a substantial force is based here, led by Grimtotem elders who are said to take their orders from Thunder Bluff.

title: Darkmist Cavern
body: Darkmist Cavern was once a mine, cut into the hills northwest of Brackenwall Village, but the miners are long gone and the darkmist spiders have taken it for themselves. Silkspinners and recluses web its tunnels, and few outside the marsh would bother them at all, except that their parts are oddly prized. The blacksmith of Brackenwall uses the acid of their venom sacs to clean burned metal, and the hermit at Swamplight Manor insists that the juice of an unpopped darkmist eye is a fine drink, smooth and salty.

title: Brackenwall Village
body: Brackenwall Village is the Horde's stronghold in Dustwallow Marsh, a rough camp of huts in the northwest where the Stonemaul ogres took refuge after black dragonkin burned them out of their southern home. Overlord Mok'Morokk rules it, though not all his ogres are content: the learned Draz'Zilb refuses to call it home, and old Tharg still mourns the wife the dragons killed. Orcs and trolls of the Horde work alongside them. Krog watches the humans for Orgrimmar, and the spymaster Nazeer Bloodpike sends agents against Theramore, whose own infiltrators spy on the village from the reeds to the east.

title: Shady Rest Inn
body: Only a blackened chimney and scattered rubble remain of the Shady Rest Inn, on the road where Dustwallow meets the Barrens. James Hyal built it, one of those who came across the sea with Lady Proudmoore, dreaming of a fine stopping place for travelers, and for a while it prospered. Then Theramore lost control of the marsh roads, and James was too stubborn to retreat behind the city's walls. The inn was burned to the ground, and his wife and son were killed. Investigators from Theramore and Brackenwall have both picked through the ashes.

Abandoned by its soldiers, it has been taken over by deserters from Theramore's own ranks, men whose loyalty to Admiral Daelin Proudmoore outlived the admiral. Young mages of both sides make the long trip into the swamp to learn from her, and her cottage stands open to anyone whose errand is pressing enough.

Drazzit Dripvalve runs the town on a tight budget and has posted a bounty on Goreclaw the Ravenous, a raptor of the Bloodfen Burrow that has killed two of his engineers. Its oddest resident is Brogg, a Stonemaul ogre who lives in the only building big enough for him and plays dice with the goblins.

Onyxia's brood has spread across it, and her eggs lie hidden among the reeds, each one another whelp to swell the dragonkin's ranks. Firemane flamecallers and scalebanes stalk the mud, the black drake Brimgore prowls the fen, and Overlord Mok'Morokk's lost strongbox lies somewhere in the muck. Bloodfen raptors and great crocolisks hunt here too, and veins of mithril and truesilver run through the hills.

title: Lady Jaina Proudmoore
body: Jaina Proudmoore, ruler of Theramore, is the daughter of Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras and was once the apprentice of Archmage Antonidas of Dalaran. When the Scourge rose, a prophet urged her to lead survivors west across the sea, and in Kalimdor she stood with Thrall and the night elves against Archimonde at Mount Hyjal. Afterward she founded Theramore. When her father came with his fleet to make war on the Horde, she would not fight beside him, and he died at her city. She has worked for peace with the Horde ever since, though some marines loyal to her father have deserted rather than serve it. Her city, she says, must come first.

He reads Orcish better than most, which makes him the man to see when a Horde spy's report turns up in the mud. Most of his days go to the mysteries of the marsh, chief among them the burning of the Shady Rest Inn, which his men have investigated with little luck. He has a soldier's dry wit about the deserters, who accuse Theramore of betraying the Alliance while they betray it themselves, and a soft spot for poor James Hyal, the innkeeper who lost everything.

title: Overlord Mok'Morokk
body: Mok'Morokk rules the Stonemaul ogres at Brackenwall Village, raised to be their overlord by Rexxar himself. Under Rexxar's eye he showed real strength, but once his patron left, power went to his head. When the black dragonkin burned the clan's old home in the south, he ordered his people to run rather than fight, and he insists that the new village is safe because there are no dragons there. He calls himself a smart ogre and a good leader, but he pines most for his grog, his snuff and his strongbox, all abandoned in the flight. Many of his ogres want revenge and their old home. He would rather stay.

body: Krog is an orc of Brackenwall Village and a shrewd agent of Orgrimmar. He boasts that the humans once claimed most of the marsh until the Stonemaul, with Horde help, pushed them back. Since the Shady Rest Inn burned he has taken a keen interest in whatever turns up in its ashes, for the Horde means to know what happened there. He has hunters like Kagoro and Ogron to track for him, knows a great many people across the Horde, and wears a set of armor the Earthen Ring gave him in thanks for some past service.

title: Tabetha
body: Tabetha keeps a little farm in the heart of the Quagmire and is far more than the old hermit she seems. She is a mage and scryer of some renown, older than she looks, and she has trained apprentices here for generations, Horde mages among them. Young mages of both sides come to her to earn a mage's wand, warlocks sent by Menara Voidrender bring her a tainted infernal orb whose demon she draws out, and she does not forgive theft: when the hydromancer Velratha of Zul'Farrak stole her Tiara of the Deep, she wanted it back badly. Both Theramore and Brackenwall trust her, and she has done more than most to keep the peace between them.

title: Brogg
body: Brogg is a Stonemaul ogre who fled with Overlord Mok'Morokk when the black dragonkin took the clan's old home, believing they would soon return to fight. The counterattack never came, and when his overlord refused to seek revenge for the friends Brogg had lost, he left Brackenwall for good. The goblins of Mudsprocket let him stay in the only building large enough to hold him, though he sometimes suspects they are laughing at him, and he trades the meat of his hunting trips at their dice table. He has never given up on his people. Brogg means to lay the Stonemaul dead to rest, avenge them, and lead the clan back where it belongs.

Master anglers of both the Horde and the Alliance are sent to his island camp in Dustwallow when their own teachers have nothing left to give, and Nat tests them with lists of rare fish from far shores. Champions seeking the Seal of Ascension come instead to break his will and forge it in his flame.

The fishmonger Dirty Michael Crowe, who collects old books, did not laugh. Sailors still spoke, he said, of Tethyr, a sea creature the book says lives right here, and old Nat Pagle would know the truth of it.

parts.body: Nat would talk only after testing a foul new bait on the visitor who asked. Then he told it plain. Tethyr was real, he lived in the waters off Theramore, he was drawn to bright light, and he was the reason the lighthouse had been shut down in the first place. Light it again, and he would come back.

title: The Brood of Onyxia
body: The Stonemaul ogres fled their village in the south when black dragons fell upon it, and at first no one in Brackenwall could say whose dragons they were. Draz'Zilb, an ogre mage as learned as he is scornful of his overlord, means to find out by casting his spells over the hearts and tongues of the whelps that now infest the old village. Overlord Mok'Morokk will hear none of it: there are no dragons in Brackenwall. Tharg, who lost his wife in the attack, wants neither spells nor talk but revenge, and sends warriors against the black dragon army in the hope of going home.

When that was done, he asked one last service. Mok'Morokk was not fit to lead, and the old warrior Tharg was too hurt and too old, so the overlord had to be driven out by force.

title: Challenge to the Black Flight
body: Brogg has waited long enough for his overlord to avenge the Stonemaul, so from Mudsprocket he means to do it himself. He left Brackenwall when Mok'Morokk would not take revenge on the black dragonkin who destroyed the clan's old home and killed many of Brogg's friends, and he has come south to lay their spirits to rest and avenge them. First he needs feathers with strong magic for his ritual, like those the raptors of the Bloodfen Burrow wear, west of town.

parts.body: Brogg's ritual needed more than feathers. The clan banner was brought out from deep in the old mound the dragonkin now call the Den of Flame, and the essences of the dragonkin who had killed his friends were gathered to feed his totem with their hate. At the Stonemaul Ruins the totem drew the restless ogre spirits from their bones so that they could be fought and laid to rest. The survivors could finally turn to the living, Brogg said, though Mok'Morokk would never give thanks. One task remained.

parts.body: Brogg's banner was carried east to the dragon's-mouth cave of the Wyrmbog and planted before Onyxia's lair as his challenge. The brood mother did not come. Her servant Smolderwing answered in her place, that Onyxia answers to no one, and Brogg decided that, like all her flight, she fights only when victory is certain. He will never give up on bringing the Stonemaul home.

title: The Last Report of Marg Nighteye
body: The Horde and Theramore keep an uneasy truce in the marsh, and Nazeer Bloodpike, the spymaster of Brackenwall, means to come out on top of it. His hunters cull the Alliance infiltrators who watch the village, and his agents dive beneath the Theramore docks for documents thrown into the sea by spies caught aboard a ship. One of his agents, Marg Nighteye, was stationed outside Theramore for weeks to spy on the city, and his reports have stopped coming. Out in the swamp, loose dirt hides more than mud.

title: The Haunting of Witch Hill
body: Mordant Grimsby, an herbalist, came out to Swamplight Manor to visit his old friend Jarl with a housewarming gift, and found him babbling about frogs in an empty cabin while the dead walked outside. It has been a nonstop horror show ever since. Mordant will not leave his friend to it. He believes that the risen husks and spirits shambling about Witch Hill must know what happened here, and that if they can be laid to rest one by one, they may give up what they know before the evil consumes Jarl.

parts.body: Mordant remembered that hedge mages use the smoke of witchbane to draw evil out of hiding. A torch bound with the herb was planted at the end of the manor's dock, and from the smoke rose Zelfrax, who claimed the land as his long before mortals came. When he fell, Mordant was almost more surprised than relieved. Jarl's taste in furniture, he admitted, remained beyond saving.
